meta.title: FORGE — Natural Bodybuilding Hypertrophy Library (Full Gym Equipment, Natty Physique Focus)

Novice.notes: Master the movement pattern and build a mind-muscle connection before chasing load. No drop sets, no training to failure. As a natural lifter you recover slower than an enhanced lifter even at this early stage — undershooting volume here is safer than overshooting it.

Beginner.notes: Standard straight-set progression. Add a paused rep on the last set of one exercise per session to reinforce the stretched position, which drives most of the hypertrophy signal.

Intermediate.intensity_isolation: RPE 8 (1-2 RIR), last set near failure
Intermediate.notes: Volume becomes the main growth lever — add a set before adding load once every prescribed rep is hit for all sets. Antagonist supersets keep session length in check as volume climbs.

Advanced.intensity_isolation: RPE 9 (0-1 RIR), rest-pause on final set
Advanced.tempo: Controlled eccentric, brief pause at stretch, controlled concentric
Advanced.notes: Natural lifters at this stage usually need LESS added volume than programs default to, not more — individualize by recovery markers (sleep, bar-speed trend, joint feel) before stacking more sets.

Elite.tempo: Autoregulated — written tempo is a floor, not a target
Elite.notes: Even at elite level, natural recovery capacity — not motivation or technique — is the ceiling on how much volume actually turns into growth. Periodize volume in waves and treat a stalling strength trend as the signal to pull back, not push through.

Full Body.description: Every major muscle group trained every session, 2-4 sessions/week.
Full Body.notes: Best default for Novice-Intermediate naturals — highest frequency per set invested, easiest to recover from as a standalone block.

Upper/Lower.description: Alternating upper-body and lower-body sessions, 4-6 sessions/week.
Upper/Lower.notes: The workhorse natural-bodybuilding split — enough per-session volume to matter, enough frequency to keep protein synthesis elevated across the week.

Push/Pull/Legs.description: Push (chest/shoulders/triceps), Pull (back/biceps), Legs, run once (3-day) or twice (6-day) per week.
Push/Pull/Legs.notes: The 3-day version trades frequency for very high single-session volume per muscle — only recommended once a lifter can recover from that in one sitting. The 6-day version is the highest-volume-tolerant natural template in this library.

Body-Part (Bro Split).description: One or two muscle groups per session, 4-6 sessions/week, each muscle typically hit once (twice on the 6-day arms/legs-specialization variants).
Body-Part (Bro Split).frequency_per_muscle: 1x per week standard (2x on specialization variants)
Body-Part (Bro Split).notes: Lets a single session go very deep on 1-2 muscles with a high exercise count — useful for advanced naturals with a specific weak point, less efficient than higher-frequency splits for a lifter without one. Include a specialization variant (2x/week on the priority muscle) rather than running every muscle at 1x/week once a lifter is advanced enough to need it.

global_rules: This library assumes a 100% natural lifter (no performance-enhancing drugs) — volume, frequency, and rest periods are calibrated to natural recovery capacity, not to what an enhanced physique-sport program would prescribe. Do not scale volume up toward bodybuilding-media norms built around enhanced recovery.
Full commercial gym on-site — all free-weight, cable/machine, and accessory equipment listed above is available without restriction; no equipment constraint applies to any template in this library.

Compound, free-weight-or-loaded-machine movements (squat/hinge/press/row/pull-up variants) stay the FIRST exercise trained for a muscle group in every session — isolation and single-joint machine work follows to finish the muscle group with controlled fatigue, never replaces the compound.

Progression rule: add ONE set to an exercise once every prescribed rep is hit for all sets at the given load; once volume caps out for the block, add load and drop back to the bottom of the rep range.

Machines and cables are the preferred tool for taking a set close to true failure (Advanced/Elite, isolation work) since they remove the stabilization demand that limits how safely a free-weight set can be pushed that far.

Deload every 5th-6th week for Novice/Beginner, every 4th-5th week for Intermediate+: cut sets by ~40-50% at the same intensity. Natural lifters accumulate fatigue slower than enhanced lifters but also dissipate it slower — do not skip deloads because a session still 'feels fine'.
Antagonist-pairing supersets (chest+back, biceps+triceps) are the default way to add training density without adding session length once superset methods are unlocked (Intermediate+).

Every working set should be trainable with visible bar-speed/rep-quality control at the prescribed RPE — grinding reps that break form do not count toward the hypertrophy stimulus and raise injury risk disproportionately for a natural lifter without the recovery buffer an enhanced lifter has.

Sleep, bodyweight trend, and daily protein intake (roughly 1.6-2.2g/kg bodyweight) are the levers that actually determine whether the volume in this library gets converted into muscle — more sets on paper cannot substitute for recovery basics.

templates.level_rules_ref: Master the movement pattern and build a mind-muscle connection before chasing load. No drop sets, no training to failure. As a natural lifter you recover slower than an enhanced lifter even at this early stage — undershooting volume here is safer than overshooting it.
templates.split_rules_ref: Lets a single session go very deep on 1-2 muscles with a high exercise count — useful for advanced naturals with a specific weak point, less efficient than higher-frequency splits for a lifter without one. Include a specialization variant (2x/week on the priority muscle) rather than running every muscle at 1x/week once a lifter is advanced enough to need it.

Include a specialization variant (2x/week on the priority muscle) rather than running every muscle at 1x/week once a lifter is advanced enough to need it.
